description: Encoding-agnostic state-transition fixtures. Opaque, frame, and commit labels assert equality only.

constraints: all state and output references resolve through reference_collections
state.observations lists only valid observations; quarantined variants appear only through quarantine records
every cursor names a position with a valid observation or a quarantine row of the same source, scope, and generation
every quarantine variant_ref is distinct from every valid observation and from other quarantine records
an atomic ingest cursor_after_ref and every item key use the ingest source, scope, and generation, else the batch is rejected

canonical_revision_output = state revisions, minus ambiguous keys (revision_conflicts), minus edits whose predecessor key is ambiguous, minus revisions with no valid observation, sorted by (order tuple, key)
a rejected or rolled-back batch leaves expected_state equal to initial_state

REVCONFLICT-E1-AUTH.reason: same CanonicalRevisionKey, different bytes and commitment, both authenticate under the owning protocol

OBSCONFLICT-R1-G1-30.reason: same ObservationKey, same position asserted for a different revision

QUAR-R2-G1-45-POISON.reason: variant failed owning-protocol validation; not an ambiguity marker

fixtures.covers: The same public E1 observed in G1 and replayed in G2.
assertions: G2 creates a second observation, not a second canonical revision
generation and source position do not affect revision identity
E1 emits once

fixtures.covers: Public E1 observed independently from R1 and R2.
assertions: relay identity occurs only in observations
R2 arrival does not reposition or re-emit E1
E1 emits once

fixtures.covers: The same object and revision ids under a different authority (A9) are a different key, not a conflict.
assertions: authority and NetworkTag are part of the key
no revision conflict and no squatting of E1 by A9

fixtures.covers: Public post E1 creation plus its edit, one logical object.
assertions: the edit has its own revision key under the same logical object
the edit is not key reuse or equivocation
order is by intrinsic tuple 10 then 11

fixtures.covers: A tombstone is a new revision with its own key under the same logical object.
assertions: the tombstone revision key differs from the create and edit keys
all revisions stay auditable; the tombstone is not physical deletion

fixtures.covers: Two private deliveries (an original and its later edit) with distinct relay-visible ids and no plaintext predecessor.
assertions: each private object is one delivery with one revision
no relay-visible field links P2 to P1; the edit relation is absent until decryption
the destination in the key is the account address (assumption #206)

fixtures.covers: An authenticated second variant under E1's existing revision key.
assertions: both variants authenticate, so the key is ambiguous and suppressed rather than selected by arrival
the ambiguity marker survives eviction of variant bytes
evidence and R2 cursor commit atomically with the conflict

fixtures.covers: A different-bytes variant of E2 that fails owning-protocol validation.
assertions: only an authenticated variant suppresses; this one is a quarantined observation on R2
no revision conflict and no ambiguity marker exist
E2 stays output regardless of arrival order

fixtures.covers: E1 and its dependent edit were emitted; an authenticated variant of E1 then arrives.
assertions: the view retracts REV-E1 and the withheld REV-E1-EDIT
the edit is reported blocked, not dropped
value-bearing consumers read only this reduced view

fixtures.covers: Same ObservationKey (R1, S1, G1, position 30) reused to assert a different revision (E1 instead of E2).
assertions: the conflicting observation is stored as a separate quarantined variant
the first valid row stays valid and the key is not ambiguous
E1 is seen only via a quarantined observation, so it is not output-eligible
the cursor stays at the last recorded position 30

fixtures.covers: An R2 batch carries an item whose ObservationKey names source R1.
assertions: item key source, scope, and generation must equal the authenticated batch
nothing is persisted under R1's identity and no cursor moves

fixtures.covers: A two-item batch whose second item fails to write.
assertions: the first item and the cursor roll back with the failed second item
after restart the batch is replayed as a first ingest

fixtures.covers: The recipient unlocks both persisted private deliveries.
assertions: only replaceable local projections change
the edit relation appears only in the decrypted local projection
revision and observation commitments and the cursor are unchanged
no canonical revision is emitted a second time

fixtures.covers: Restart reconstructs state, then receives an identical retry.
assertions: restart output is derived only from persisted records
the identical retry adds no row, conflict, or output (equal commitments)
E1 emits at most once

fixtures.covers: Restart from a state holding a quarantined variant, then the identical variant is retried.
assertions: output after restart equals output before it
the identical quarantined variant creates no new quarantine row
E1 stays output-ineligible and E2 stays valid
